notes: Second full sweep at db91c23: five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the tool calls are Read, Write, Edit and Bash only), and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. Expected reads (testing.md and processes.md) is therefore unmet in every run, as expected for baseline.

Changed rule, graded against the current text of references/testing.md: "Group tests by function and name them by behaviour". Deciding sentences: "Name a `describe` block after the function under test, or after a condition its tests share", "A block that joins two functions (`describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2"`) no longer says which one a failure is about." and "`test "returns :ok"` states a return value most functions share, so a failure line names nothing". Counts: a block joining two functions in 4 of 5 runs (opus-1 line 56, haiku-1 line 32, sonnet-1 line 65, sonnet-2 line 52, each describe "subscribe/3 and subscribers/2" do); a test name stating only its return value in 1 of 5 (sonnet-2 line 94: test "returns :ok even with no subscribers", graded as the previous sweep graded "returns :ok for a pid"). A condition describe, now allowed, appears in 5 of 5 (describe "when a subscribed process exits" do at opus-1 line 139, haiku-1 line 118, haiku-2 line 153, sonnet-1 line 217, sonnet-2 line 168); under the 93873be text these were the violations, so haiku-2 is clean only because of the change. Previous sweep: 5 of 5 baseline runs violated.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Start processes with `start_supervised!/1`". Deciding sentences: "To assert that a start fails, call `start_supervised/1` and match the reason." and "a server that registers `__MODULE__` by default takes a test-specific name built from the context's module and test name, `Module.concat(context.module, context.test)`." Counts for the first: start_link called from a test to assert the missing-mailer failure in 4 of 5 runs (haiku-1 line 173, haiku-2 line 38, sonnet-1 line 61, sonnet-2 lines 47-48); opus-1 uses start_supervised/2 and matches the KeyError reason (lines 51-52). Counts for the second: a name built with Module.concat(context.module, context.test) in 0 of 5; a name that is not test-specific in 1 of 5 (sonnet-1 line 26, one fixed :subscriptions_under_test for every test). opus-1 passes name: nil (no name, which "or none" allows); haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 use System.unique_integer atoms, unique per test but not built from the context. I graded those clean, as the previous sweep graded unique names, because the rule's stated reason (async tests colliding on a global name) cannot arise; reading the sentence as requiring the context-built name would add these three to the count (4 of 5) but change no verdict, since all three already call start_link. Previous sweep: 3 of 5 baseline runs violated.

Judgment on the same rule that decides opus-1's verdict: 4 of 5 runs start a server under the default name Notify.Subscriptions to test that default (opus-1 line 223, haiku-2 lines 28-29, sonnet-1 line 54, sonnet-2 line 86), each inside an async: false module. I did not count these, because the test's subject is the default name and the concurrency rule names "named singleton processes" as a reason for async: false, so no async test can collide. opus-1 alone moves that test into its own async: false module (lines 216-218) and keeps the main module async: true. If the name sentence is read to cover these starts too, opus-1 becomes violated on this rule; the other three are violated already.

Changed rule, graded against the current text: "Run tests concurrently unless they share global state". Deciding sentence: "`Process.register(self(), TestMailer)` and `Application.put_env(:notify, :test_pid, self())` make the test process a singleton, which forces `async: false`." Counts: Process.register on the test pid with async: false in 4 of 5 runs (haiku-1 line 28, haiku-2 line 19, sonnet-1 line 25, sonnet-2 line 24); Application.put_env in 0 of 5 (both sonnet runs used it in the previous sweep); a Registry keyed by the server's test-specific name in 0 of 5. opus-1 keeps async: true by registering the test process in a Registry under a fresh email address per test (lines 184-188), which the mailer double looks up (line 12). That is not the key the rule shows, but it uses no global state and forces nothing, so it is graded clean. Previous sweep: 4 of 5 baseline runs violated.

Unchanged rules follow the 2026-10-21 standard. "Wait for messages, not for time" is violated in 5 of 5: every run polls the subscriber list with Process.sleep in a retry helper after an exit; sonnet-2 waits for the exiting process's :DOWN first (line 40) but still polls. opus-1 moves from clean in the previous sweep to violated. "Assert with patterns": sonnet-1 asserts with is_pid (lines 50, 55), the construct the previous sweep counted against sonnet-1. "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Use setup for shared data" are clean in all five.

Tests were run from copies in the scratch folder with elixir -r test-writing-input.ex subscriptions_test.exs, five times each, each with a new random seed; every run passed every time with no compiler warnings (opus-1 14 tests, haiku-1 16, haiku-2 21, sonnet-1 26, sonnet-2 22). mix format --check-formatted on the copies confirms format_ok in result.json: haiku-1 fails on line 179 (102 characters) and sonnet-1 on lines 26, 40-41, 236 and 241; the other three pass.
